title: Purpose of the risk practice
blurb: Explain why PRINCE2 manages risk: to identify, assess and control uncertainty so the project is more likely to succeed.
question: Which is the purpose of the risk practice: to guarantee the objectives are met, or to improve the project's ability to succeed by controlling uncertainty?

teach.body: Formally: the risk practice exists to identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect the project's objectives, and so improve the project's ability to succeed. In plain English: every project faces things that might or might not happen. Rather than hoping for the best, PRINCE2 spots them early, sizes them up and acts on them, so success becomes more likely. It cannot promise success.

teach.caption: Learn the three verbs: identify, assess, control. The object is uncertainty that would affect objectives.

teach.body: A risk is an uncertain event or set of events that, should it occur, will affect the achievement of objectives. It is measured by combining the probability of it happening with the size of its impact on objectives. Note the word 'uncertain': if something has already happened or is certain, it is not a risk but an issue.

teach.caption: PRINCE2 uses 'risk' for both. Opportunities are not an afterthought.

teach.h: Is it a risk at all?
Why it matters to the whole project
teach.body: Projects are riskier than business as usual because they bring change and uncertainty. The business case weighs benefits against costs and associated risks, so risk feeds straight into the question 'is this still worth doing?'. Risk is also one of the seven aspects of performance, so the board can set a risk tolerance and use manage by exception for risk.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a depot electrification project
teach.body: At Larchfield Buses, project manager Tomasz Nowak is starting a project to install charging points at two depots. He notes that the grid connection might be delayed (a threat) and that a government grant scheme might reopen (an opportunity). Neither has happened yet. He records both, assesses them against the time and cost objectives and plans responses. He tells the board this improves their chances, not that it guarantees the go-live date.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) The purpose is to IMPROVE the ability to succeed; it cannot guarantee objectives. (2) Risk covers opportunities as well as threats. (3) A problem that has already happened is an issue for the issues practice, not a risk.

items: Purpose: identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect objectives.
Result: improves the project's ability to succeed; no guarantee.
A risk is uncertain, measured by probability and impact.
Threats are negative, opportunities positive; both are risks.
Something certain or already happened is an issue, not a risk.

summary: You can now state the purpose of the risk practice: to identify, assess and control uncertainty that would affect the project's objectives, improving its ability to succeed. You can also explain that risk includes both threats and opportunities and is different from an issue.

A.q: Which is the purpose of the risk practice?
options: To identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect objectives
To collect and assess issues and control changes to the project baseline
To ensure the agreed objectives are met by removing the project threats
To describe the quality techniques and standards to be applied to products
A.why: The risk practice identifies, assesses and controls uncertainties that would affect the project's objectives, so improving its ability to succeed (manual 9.1).

whyNot.1: That is the purpose of the issues practice.
whyNot.2: Risk management improves the ability to succeed; it cannot ensure objectives are met, and it covers opportunities as well as threats.
whyNot.3: That describes the quality management approach.

A.q: Which term does PRINCE2 use for an uncertain event that would have a positive effect on objectives?
options: Benefit
Opportunity
Outcome
Concession
A.why: PRINCE2 calls an uncertain event with a positive impact an opportunity, and one with a negative impact a threat.

whyNot.0: A benefit is a measurable improvement from an outcome, not an uncertain event.
whyNot.2: An outcome is the result of change, not an uncertain event.
whyNot.3: A concession is an accepted off-specification.

A.q: A risk is measured by a combination of which two things?
options: Its cost and the time it would take to fix
Its owner and the action owner assigned to it
Its probability and the size of its impact
Its cause and the date it was registered
A.why: A risk is measured by combining the probability of it occurring with the magnitude of its impact on objectives.

whyNot.0: Cost and time are objectives a risk can affect, not the measure of the risk itself.
whyNot.1: Owners are responsibilities for responding, not measures of the risk.
whyNot.3: The cause helps describe the risk; the registration date is administrative.

B.q:
Which two statements about the risk practice are correct?
1. It aims to improve the project's ability to succeed.
2. It covers threats and opportunities.
3. It ensures the agreed objectives will be met.
4. It deals with events that have already happened.
options: 1 and 3
2 and 4
1 and 2
3 and 4
B.why: The practice improves the ability to succeed (1) and covers both threats and opportunities (2).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is false: objectives cannot be guaranteed.
whyNot.1: Statement 4 is false: events that have happened are issues.
whyNot.3: Both are false: no guarantee is possible, and past events are issues.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. A risk is an [?] event or set of events that, should it occur, will affect the achievement of objectives.
options: adverse
unplanned
external
uncertain
B.why: Uncertainty is the defining feature of a risk; once it is certain it becomes an issue.

whyNot.0: Risks can be positive (opportunities), so 'adverse' is too narrow.
whyNot.1: Planned activities can carry risks; the defining feature is uncertainty.
whyNot.2: Risks can arise inside or outside the project.

B.q: A supplier has just told the project manager that a delivery has arrived damaged. How should this be treated?
options: As an issue, because it has already happened
As a threat, because its effect is negative
As an opportunity, because it can be claimed back
As a risk cause, recorded in the risk management approach
B.why: The damage has already occurred, so it is an event needing management consideration: an issue, not a risk.

whyNot.1: A threat is uncertain; this event is already certain.
whyNot.2: A possible insurance claim does not make the damaged delivery an uncertain positive event.
whyNot.3: The risk management approach holds procedures, not specific situations.

C.q: Which practice manages a possible future delay, and where would it be recorded?
options: The issues practice, in the issue register
The progress practice, in the daily log
The risk practice, in the risk register
The plans practice, in the stage plan
C.why: A possible future delay is uncertain, so it is a risk managed by the risk practice and recorded in the risk register.

whyNot.0: The issues practice handles events that have happened or are certain.
whyNot.1: The daily log holds informal issues and notes; formal risks go in the risk register.
whyNot.3: Plans may reflect risk responses, but the risk itself is recorded in the risk register.

C.q: Why does the risk practice support the ensure continued business justification principle?
options: The business case weighs benefits against costs and associated risks
The business case sets the risk tolerance for each work package
The business case lists the risk owner for every identified threat
The business case replaces the risk register during initiation
C.why: Justification depends on expected benefits outweighing costs and associated risks, so the risk picture feeds the business case.

whyNot.1: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager in the work package description, not by the business case.
whyNot.2: Risk owners are recorded in the risk register.
whyNot.3: The risk register records risks throughout the project; nothing replaces it.

C.q: Which statement best links the risk practice to manage by exception?
options: Risk is reviewed at each stage boundary before the next stage
Risk is one of the seven aspects for which tolerance is set
Risk lessons are passed on to future projects in a report
Risk responses are owned by the person best placed to act
C.why: Risk is one of the seven aspects of performance, so a risk tolerance can be set and escalation follows a forecast breach.

whyNot.0: Reviewing at stage boundaries links risk to manage by stages.
whyNot.2: Passing on lessons links risk to learn from experience.
whyNot.3: Assigning owners is part of the implement step, not the link to manage by exception.

reteach.title: Planning a family road trip
reteach.question: You might hit traffic, and you might find a cheaper ferry. Why plan for both before setting off?

blocks.body: Traffic is a threat: it might happen and would make you late. A cheaper ferry is an opportunity: it might happen and would save money. You check the route, judge how likely each is and decide what to do. You cannot guarantee a perfect trip, but you improve your chances. That is the risk practice: identify, assess and control uncertainty to improve the ability to succeed.

blocks.text: A flat tyre you already have is not a risk: it has happened, so it is an issue to deal with now.

explain.body: Identify, assess and control uncertainties that would affect objectives, improving the project's ability to succeed.

test.q: What is the result the risk practice aims for?
options: A guarantee that time and cost targets are met
An improved ability for the project to succeed
A full list of every possible project event
A smaller budget because threats are removed
test.why: Controlling uncertainty improves the project's ability to succeed; it cannot guarantee objectives.

whyNot.0: No practice can guarantee objectives will be met.
whyNot.2: The aim is to manage the uncertainties that matter, not list every event.
whyNot.3: Some responses cost money; the aim is success, not a smaller budget.

explain.body: A threat is an uncertain event with a negative effect; an opportunity is one with a positive effect. Both are risks.

test.q: What is a threat in PRINCE2?
options: An event that has damaged a product
A request to change an approved baseline
A forecast breach of stage tolerance
An uncertain event with a negative effect
test.why: A threat is an uncertain event that would have a negative impact on objectives.

whyNot.0: An event that has already happened is an issue.
whyNot.1: That is a request for change, a type of issue.
whyNot.2: A forecast tolerance breach is an exception.

explain.body: Uncertain and in the future: risk. Already happened or certain: issue.

test.q: The team has just found that a key supplier has gone out of business. What is this?
options: An issue
A threat
A risk cause
An opportunity
test.why: It has already happened, so it is an issue requiring management consideration.

whyNot.1: A threat is uncertain; this has already happened.
whyNot.2: It may give rise to new risks, but the event itself needs handling now as an issue.
whyNot.3: An opportunity is an uncertain positive event.

explain.body: Probability (how likely) combined with impact (how big the effect on objectives).

test.q: Which pair is used to measure a risk?
options: Owner and action owner
Cause and effect
Probability and impact
Appetite and tolerance
test.why: A risk is measured by combining probability with the magnitude of impact.

whyNot.1: Cause and effect describe the risk; they do not measure it.
whyNot.3: Appetite and tolerance set limits for risk taking, not the size of one risk.
